issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a subroutine named set_pixel to be implemented and called from main, but the solution implementation defines a function named write_pixel and does not provide a set_pixel label. The solution still calls set_pixel from main, creating an unresolved/missing symbol and a mismatch between the expected subroutine name and the one provided. This prevents the solution from matching the template's expected structure and will cause confusion or build/link errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the solution provides a set_pixel subroutine that matches the name used in main (or change the call in main to the implemented name). Rename write_pixel to set_pixel, or add a small set_pixel wrapper that forwards to write_pixel while preserving the required register behavior. Verify the subroutine preserves registers per the specification (only eax may be changed) and that symbol names match the template and problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template explicitly refer to the subroutine name set_pixel, but the solution implements the same functionality under the different identifier write_pixel (and also still calls set_pixel). This mismatch prevents a clear mapping from the exercise requirement (implement set_pixel) to the provided solution implementation and may confuse students looking for the required routine or trying to compare template and solution code.

Rename the solution's write_pixel to set_pixel (or add a set_pixel wrapper that calls write_pixel) so the template stub, the problem statement, and the solution use the identical name set_pixel.
